payload:
Augmented Expense Analysis — Q2 2026 (for Tax Review)

Summary:
- Total expenses: $73,000.

Line-item comments (tax-relevant):
1) Salaries & Benefits — $40,000 (54.8%)
   - Comment: Engineering and operations payroll; primary labor cost.
   - Tax notes: Generally deductible as ordinary business expense; employer payroll taxes and benefits are deductible; portions of wages attributable to qualified R&D activities may qualify for R&D tax credits and should be documented via timesheets/project allocation.
   - Recommended tag: Deductible (portion = payroll taxes deductible); R&D-allocatable wages -> Document & Flag for R&D credit.

2) R&D — $15,000 (20.5%)
   - Comment: Product development and research expenditures.
   - Tax notes: Candidate for R&D tax credit if activities meet qualified research criteria; some costs (especially software development for internal-use software) may require capitalization under applicable accounting rules—evaluate per capital vs. current expense guidance.
   - Recommended tag: Review for R&D tax credit; consider capitalization review for internal-use software costs; maintain project documentation and time tracking.

3) Marketing — $10,000 (13.7%)
   - Comment: Campaigns and promotional spend.
   - Tax notes: Typically deductible as advertising/marketing expense when incurred; certain customer-acquisition costs may be subject to capitalization under specific accounting rules—confirm materiality and policy.
   - Recommended tag: Deductible; retain invoices and performance metrics; flag any large customer-acquisition spend for capitalization policy review.

4) Office & Utilities — $5,000 (6.8%)
   - Comment: Rent, utilities, office supplies.
   - Tax notes: Rent and utilities are ordinarily deductible; leasehold improvements should be capitalized and depreciated; supplies are deductible unless part of a capital project.
   - Recommended tag: Deductible (except leasehold improvements -> Capitalize & depreciate).

5) Miscellaneous — $3,000 (4.1%)
   - Comment: Travel, subscriptions, sundry expenses.
   - Tax notes: Travel and business subscriptions are generally deductible (subject to substantiation and any entertainment limitations); ensure receipts and business purpose documentation.
   - Recommended tag: Deductible; require receipts and business-purpose notes.

Explicit tax-related observations / action items:
- R&D tax credit potential: R&D spend ($15k) appears to be a material candidate; require project descriptions, employee time allocation, invoices for contract research, and evidence of technical uncertainty and experimentation to support a credit claim.
- Capitalization risk: Review whether any portion of R&D or marketing relates to capital projects (internal-use software, significant customer-acquisition programs, or leasehold improvements). If so, reclassify and apply capitalization/depreciation rules.
- Payroll taxes & compliance: Employer payroll tax expense is deductible but requires correct classification and remittance records; ensure payroll tax accruals and withholdings are up to date.
- Documentation requirements: For audit-readiness and TaxVerifier review, collect supporting docs (timesheets, vendor invoices, contracts, receipts, project narratives) and map costs to GL accounts.

Short recommended treatment for reporting/tax purposes:
- Immediate reporting: Classify Salaries, Marketing, Office & Utilities, Miscellaneous as deductible operating expenses in the reporting period, unless specific costs meet capitalization thresholds.
- R&D: Segregate R&D costs into a dedicated sub-ledger and prepare supporting documentation to evaluate R&D tax credit eligibility; if internal-use software criteria met, apply capitalization rules to that portion.
- Accounting/tax controls: Implement a simple tagging scheme in the general ledger for each expense line: {TaxTreatment: Deductible | CapitalizePendingReview | R&D_Credit_Candidate} and attach source documents.
- Next step: Submit this augmented analysis and supporting documentation to TaxVerifier for explicit approval of tax treatment and to determine any follow-up audit by TaxSpecialist if required.

Note: This analysis is prepared for submission to TaxVerifier; please confirm if you want a separate spreadsheet of line-item mappings and supporting-document checklist.
